solution_steps.issue: The appliance does not operate if the plug or cord is damaged, and it must be replaced by Kenwood or an authorized repairer.
solution_steps.steps:
1. If the plug or cord is damaged it must, for safety reasons, be replaced by Kenwood or an authorised Kenwood repairer in order to avoid a hazard.
2. If the plug or cord requires replacing a new cord set should be fitted by an Authorised Kenwood Repairer.
3. For non-rewireable plugs the fuse cover MUST be refitted when replacing the fuse. If the fuse cover is lost then the plug must not be used until a replacement can be obtained. The correct fuse cover is identified by colour and a replacement may be obtained from your Kenwood Authorised Repairer.
4. If a non-rewireable plug is cut off it must be DESTROYED IMMEDIATELY. An electric shock hazard may arise if an unwanted non-rewireable plug is inadvertently inserted into a socket outlet.
5. If you need help with servicing, spare parts or repairs (in or out of guarantee), call Kenwood customer care on 0345 222 0458 in the UK. Have your model number (e.g. TYPE: FDP65) and date code (5 digit code e.g. 21T04) ready. They are on the underside of the power unit.
6. For other countries, if you experience any problems with the operation of your appliance, before requesting assistance refer to the ‘Troubleshooting Guide’ section in the manual or visit www.kenwoodworld.com.

solution_steps.issue: Users might encounter a scald risk if hot ingredients are processed, as the appliance is not designed to handle hot ingredients.
solution_steps.steps:
1. DO NOT process hot ingredients.
2. SCALD RISK: Hot ingredients must be allowed to cool to room temperature before placing in the goblet/bottle or before blending.
3. Be careful if hot liquid is poured into the food processor or blender as it can be ejected out of the appliance due to sudden steaming.

solution_steps.issue: The appliance may be damaged if operated continuously for longer than the recommended times in the usage chart.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Refer to the "recommended usage chart" for the specific maximum operation time for each function or attachment. For example, the Blender/Blend-Xtract 2GO has a maximum operation time of 60 seconds.

2. After using the appliance for the specified maximum operation time, unplug the appliance and allow it to cool down for the rest period mentioned in the chart. For instance, after using the Blender/Blend-Xtract 2GO for 60 seconds, allow it to cool down for 15 minutes.

3. Do not exceed the maximum capacities stated in the recommended usage chart to prevent damage.

4. Always switch off the appliance and disconnect from the supply if it is left unattended.

5. Ensure that you do not process hot ingredients, as this can damage the appliance.

6. Verify that you are not using an unauthorized attachment, as this can cause damage.

7. Ensure the interlock mechanism is not subjected to excessive force, as this can damage the appliance.

8. Avoid leaving the appliance unattended when it is operating to prevent potential damage.

solution_steps.issue: The mini chopper/mill attachment may draw the maximum load, causing the appliance to overheat if used improperly.
solution_steps.steps:
1 Put the ingredients into the jar.
2 Fit the sealing ring into the blade assembly.
3 Turn the blade assembly upside down. Lower it into the jar, blades down.
4 Screw the blade assembly onto the jar until finger tight. Refer to the graphics on the underside of the blade assembly as follows: - Unlocked position - Locked position.
5 Place the mill onto the power unit and turn clockwise to lock in position.
6 Select Maximum speed or use the pulse (P).
7 Never fit the blade assembly to the power unit without the jar/lid fitted.
8 Never unscrew the jar/lid while the mill is fitted to your appliance.
9 Do not touch the sharp blades – Keep the blade assembly away from children.
10 Never remove the mill until the blades have completely stopped.
11 Do not process hot ingredients in the mill; allow to cool down to room temperature before processing.

solution_steps.issue: Failure to comply with the instructions for domestic use may result in the appliance malfunctioning or Kenwood not accepting liability.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Only use the appliance for its intended domestic use. Kenwood will not accept any liability if the appliance is subject to improper use, or failure to comply with these instructions."
2. "This appliance shall not be used by children. Keep the appliance and its cord out of reach of children."
3. "Appliances can be used by persons with reduced physical, sensory or mental capabilities or lack of experience and knowledge if they have been given supervision or instruction concerning use of the appliance in a safe way and if they understand the hazards involved."
4. "Misuse of your processor, blender or mill can result in injury."
5. "The maximum rating is based on the mini chopper/mill attachment that draws the greatest load. Other attachments may draw less power."
6. "DO NOT touch the sharp blades. The blades and discs are very sharp, handle with care. Always hold by the finger grip at the top, away from the cutting edge, when handling the sharp cutting blades, emptying the bowl and during cleaning."
7. "DO NOT process hot ingredients."
8. "Be careful if hot liquid is poured into the food processor or blender as it can be ejected out of the appliance due to sudden steaming."
9. "Never leave the appliance unattended when it is operating."
10. "Do not exceed the maximum capacities stated in the recommended usage chart."
11. "Do not operate your appliance for longer than the times specified below without a rest period. Processing continuously for longer periods can damage your appliance."

solution_steps.issue: The appliance may eject hot liquid if poured in quickly, due to sudden steaming, posing a risk of injury.
solution_steps.steps:
1. DO NOT process hot ingredients.
2. SCALD RISK: Hot ingredients must be allowed to cool to room temperature before placing in the goblet/bottle or before blending.
3. Be careful if hot liquid is poured into the food processor or blender as it can be ejected out of the appliance due to sudden steaming.

solution_steps.issue: Children cannot use the appliance, and it must be kept out of their reach, which may limit household convenience.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "This appliance shall not be used by children. Keep the appliance and its cord out of reach of children."
2. "Children should be supervised to ensure that they do not play with the appliance."
3. "Always switch off the appliance and disconnect from the supply if it is left unattended and before assembling, disassembling or cleaning."
4. "Never let the power unit, cord or plug get wet."
5. "Do not let excess cord hang over the edge of a table or worktop or touch hot surfaces."

solution_steps.issue: The blades and discs are very sharp, increasing the risk of injury if not handled with care during cleaning or handling.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Read these instructions carefully and retain for future reference.
2. DO NOT touch the sharp blades. The blades and discs are very sharp, handle with care. Always hold by the finger grip at the top, away from the cutting edge, when handling the sharp cutting blades, emptying the bowl and during cleaning.
3. Switch off the appliance and disconnect from the supply before assembling, disassembling or cleaning.
4. Wait until the attachment/blades have completely stopped before handling.
5. Be careful not to unscrew the bottle or mill jar/lid from the blade assembly.
6. Never use your fingers to push food down the feed tube. Always use the pusher supplied.
7. Store your discs, emulsifying disc and dough tool in the bag supplied. For safety reason the knife blade should be stored securely.

solution_steps.issue: Exceeding the maximum capacities stated in the recommended usage chart can lead to appliance damage.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Do not exceed the maximum capacities stated in the chart below."
2. Refer to the "Recommended Usage Chart" in the manual to determine the maximum capacity for the specific function or attachment you are using.
3. "Remove all packaging and any labels" from the appliance before use.
4. Always "use the appliance for its intended domestic use."
5. If you need to process larger quantities, split the ingredients into multiple batches to stay within the recommended capacities.
6. "Do not operate your appliance for longer than the times specified below without a rest period."
7. Ensure that you "unplug the appliance and allow to cool down for 15 minutes" if you have reached the maximum operation time.
8. "Never leave the appliance unattended when it is operating."
9. "Always switch off the appliance and disconnect from the supply if it is left unattended and before assembling, disassembling or cleaning."

solution_steps.issue: Users may face difficulty if they lack the supervision or instruction necessary for safe appliance use, especially those with reduced physical, sensory, or mental capabilities.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Appliances can be used by persons with reduced physical, sensory, or mental capabilities or lack of experience and knowledge if they have been given supervision or instruction concerning use of the appliance in a safe way and if they understand the hazards involved.
2. Keep the appliance and its cord out of reach of children.
3. Only use the appliance for its intended domestic use.
4. Never use an unauthorised attachment.
5. Never use a damaged appliance. Get it checked or repaired: see ‘service and customer care’.
6. Always switch off the appliance and disconnect from the supply if it is left unattended and before assembling, disassembling or cleaning.

issues: Blender overheats and shuts off due to Automatic Overload Protection when blending at low speed for too long.
Blender does not operate when the lid and lid plug are not securely in place.
The motor fails to cool properly when not using High speed, leading to potential overheating.
Food fails to circulate in the blender, causing the machine to stall or become overloaded.
Difficulty in releasing trapped air bubbles, which affects blending efficiency.
Machine malfunctions or fails to operate due to a damaged cord or plug.
Risk of electrical shock if the blender base is submerged in water or other liquid.
Blender does not turn on or off properly if plugged into an ungrounded outlet.
Appliance may pose a safety risk if used unattended, particularly near children or incapacitated individuals.
Risk of burns or scalding when blending hot liquids or ingredients without proper precautions.

solution_steps.issue: Blender overheats and shuts off due to Automatic Overload Protection when blending at low speed for too long.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Refer to the tip in the manual: "Blending too long at too low a speed setting will overheat the machine and cause the Automatic Overload Protection to turn the machine off." To prevent overheating, use the High speed as often as possible to achieve the most uniform consistency and maximize the motor’s cooling fan.

2. If the Automatic Overload Protection is activated and the blender shuts off, the manual states: "When engaged, this Automatic Overload Protection will cause the motor to shut off and possibly emit a light odor." 

3. To reset your machine after Automatic Overload Protection is activated, refer to the manual: "If your Automatic Overload Protection should ever be activated, refer to page 7 in this manual to easily reset your machine."

4. To prevent "overloading" your Vitamix machine in the future, follow these additional tips from the manual:
   - "Process only Vitamix recipes when learning to use the machine."
   - "Do not process recipes at lower speeds than recommended."
   - "Do not process recipes longer than recommended."
   - "Use your tamper to process thicker mixtures and keep ingredients moving around and through the blades."

solution_steps.issue: Blender does not operate when the lid and lid plug are not securely in place.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Read all instructions, safeguards, and warnings before operating blender.

2. Always operate blender with lid and lid plug firmly in place. The lid plug should be removed only when adding ingredients and when using the tamper.

3. To lock the lid in place: Position lid on container with lid flaps midway between the spout and the handle. Push the lid onto the container until it locks in place.

4. The lid must always be secured when processing, especially hot liquids that may scald.

solution_steps.issue: The motor fails to cool properly when not using High speed, leading to potential overheating.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "tIP: Blending too long at too low a speed setting will overheat the machine and cause the Automatic Overload Protection to turn the machine off. Use the High () speed as often as possible to achieve the most uniform consistency."
2. "Blending on High () speed also maximizes the motor’s cooling fan to avoid overheating."
3. "If the food does not circulate, the machine may be overloaded or may have trapped an air bubble. Carefully remove the lid plug while making sure the lid stays firmly in place."
4. "Release the air bubble by inserting the tamper through the lid plug opening."
5. "If circulation problems continue, reduce the machine speed. A lower speed may allow food to circulate when a higher speed does not."
6. "Once the food is circulating freely, increase the speed back to High () and continue processing."

solution_steps.issue: Food fails to circulate in the blender, causing the machine to stall or become overloaded.
solution_steps.steps:
1. If the food fails to circulate, carefully remove the lid plug while making sure the lid stays firmly in place. Release the air bubble by inserting the tamper through the lid plug opening.
2. If circulation problems continue, reduce the machine speed. A lower speed may allow food to circulate when a higher speed does not.
3. Once the food is circulating freely, increase the speed back to High and continue processing.
4. Ensure the container is not more than two-thirds full when using the tamper during blending.
5. Do not use the tamper for more than 30 consecutive seconds to avoid overheating.

solution_steps.issue: Difficulty in releasing trapped air bubbles, which affects blending efficiency.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Carefully remove the lid plug while making sure the lid stays firmly in place.
2. Release the air bubble by inserting the tamper through the lid plug opening.
3. Use the tamper to press ingredients into the blades as you make frozen ice creams and nut butters, or purée fruits and vegetables.
4. If circulation problems continue, reduce the machine speed. A lower speed may allow food to circulate when a higher speed does not. Once the food is circulating freely, increase the speed back to High and continue processing.

solution_steps.issue: Machine malfunctions or fails to operate due to a damaged cord or plug.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Do not operate any appliance with a damaged cord or plug or after the appliance malfunctions, or is dropped or damaged in any manner.
2. Call Vitamix Customer Service at 1-800-848-2649 or 1-440-235-4840 or email service@vitamix.com at once for examination, repair, replacement, or electrical.

solution_steps.issue: Risk of electrical shock if the blender base is submerged in water or other liquid.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Read all instructions, safeguards, and warnings before operating the blender.
2. To protect against the risk of electrical shock, do not put the blender base in water or other liquid.
3. Unplug from outlet when not in use, before putting on or taking off parts, and before cleaning.
4. Do not operate any appliance with a damaged cord or plug or after the appliance malfunctions, or is dropped or damaged in any manner. Call Vitamix Customer Service at 1-800-848-2649 or 1-440-235-4840 or email service@vitamix.com at once for examination, repair, replacement, or electrical adjustment.
5. Electrical Shock Hazard. Use grounded outlet only. Do not remove ground. Do not use an adapter. Do not use an extension cord. Failure to follow instructions can cause death or electrical shock.

solution_steps.issue: Blender does not turn on or off properly if plugged into an ungrounded outlet.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Ensure the power switch is set to Off (O) as stated: "Make sure that the power switch is set to Off (O)."

2. Confirm that the machine is plugged into a grounded electrical outlet: "Use grounded outlet only."

3. If the machine is not turning on, check if the reset button needs to be pressed: "220 Volt machines: 220/240 motors are equipped with a reset button. If the motor shuts off, press the black reset button on the bottom of the machine."

4. Ensure that you are not using an adapter or extension cord: "Do not use an adapter. Do not use an extension cord."

5. If the issue persists, contact Vitamix Customer Service for further assistance: "Call Vitamix Customer Service at 1-800-848-2649 or 1-440-235-4840 or email service@vitamix.com at once for examination, repair, replacement, or electrical."

solution_steps.issue: Appliance may pose a safety risk if used unattended, particularly near children or incapacitated individuals.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Read all instructions, safeguards, and warnings before operating the blender.

2. Not intended for use by or near children or persons with reduced physical, sensory, or mental capabilities or lack of experience and knowledge.

3. Close supervision is necessary when any appliance is used by or near children or incapacitated persons.

4. Do not leave your Vitamix blender unattended when operating.

5. Always operate blender with lid and lid plug firmly in place. The lid plug should be removed only when adding ingredients and when using the tamper.

solution_steps.issue: Risk of burns or scalding when blending hot liquids or ingredients without proper precautions.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Read and understand the instruction manual before using this machine.
2. When blending hot liquids or ingredients, use caution; spray or escaping steam may cause scalding and burns.
3. Do not fill the container to the maximum capacity.
4. Always begin processing on the lowest speed.
5. Never start on speeds above 1 with hot liquids to avoid possible burns.
6. Lock the lid. This will prevent expansion from affecting the position of the lid when the machine is turned on.
7. Start on Variable 1, slowly increase to 10.
8. Always operate the blender with lid and lid plug firmly in place. The lid plug should be removed only when adding ingredients and when using the tamper.

issues: Motor doesn’t start or the blade assembly doesn’t rotate.
Food is unevenly chopped due to overloading or unevenly sized pieces.
Food is chopped too fine or becomes too watery because of over-processing.
Food collects on the lid or sides of the container, indicating the mixture is too thick.
Cannot achieve snow from solid ice when using ice that has started to melt.
Motor base won’t stick to the counter or tabletop.
The appliance does not turn on because the power button is not pressed.
The unit overheats or overloads, requiring a cooling period before reuse.
The container is not securely locked on the motor base, preventing operation.
The lid is not securely on the container in the correct position, affecting functionality.

solution_steps.issue: Motor doesn’t start or the blade assembly doesn’t rotate.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Make sure the container is securely locked on the motor base.
2. Make sure the lid is securely on the container in the correct position (align arrows).
3. The appliance is turned “Off”. Press the power button ( ) to turn “On”.
4. Check that the plug is securely inserted into the electrical outlet.
5. Check the fuse or circuit breaker.
6. The unit has overheated or overloaded. Unplug and wait approximately 15 minutes before using again.
7. Check to make sure the unit is not overloaded.

solution_steps.issue: Food is unevenly chopped due to overloading or unevenly sized pieces.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Either you are chopping too much food at one time, or the pieces are not of even size and processing smaller amounts per batch.
2. Pulse ingredients for even chopping by pressing down in short intervals.

solution_steps.issue: Food is chopped too fine or becomes too watery because of over-processing.
solution_steps.steps: 1. The food has been over processed. Use pulse button for controlled processing.

solution_steps.issue: Food collects on the lid or sides of the container, indicating the mixture is too thick.
solution_steps.steps:
1. The mixture is too thick. Add more liquid.
2. If you find unmixed ingredients sticking to the sides of the pitcher, stop the appliance, remove the lid, and use a spatula to dislodge ingredients. NEVER insert your hands into the pitcher, as you may contact one of the blades and experience a laceration.
3. DO NOT attempt to remove the container or lid from the motor base while the blade assembly is still spinning. Allow the appliance to come to a complete stop before doing so.

solution_steps.issue: Cannot achieve snow from solid ice when using ice that has started to melt.
solution_steps.steps:
1. DO NOT use ice that has been sitting out or has started to melt. Use ice straight from the freezer.
2. Start with a few pulses and then go to a continuous blending cycle.

solution_steps.issue: Motor base won’t stick to the counter or tabletop.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Make sure surface and suction feet are wiped clean.
2. Suction feet will only stick to smooth surfaces.
3. Suction feet WILL NOT stick on some surfaces such as wood, tile, and non-polished finishes.
4. DO NOT attempt to use appliance when the motor base is stuck to a surface that is not secure, (cutting board, platter, plates, etc.).

solution_steps.issue: The appliance does not turn on because the power button is not pressed.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Make sure the container is securely locked on the motor base.
2. Make sure the lid is securely on the container in the correct position (align arrows).
3. The appliance is turned “Off”. Press the power button ( ) to turn “On”.
4. Check that the plug is securely inserted into the electrical outlet.
5. Check the fuse or circuit breaker.

solution_steps.issue: The unit overheats or overloads, requiring a cooling period before reuse.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Unplug the unit from the electrical outlet.
2. Allow the unit to cool for approximately 15 minutes.
3. Remove the container’s lid and blade assembly. Empty the container and ensure no ingredients are jamming the blade assembly.
4. IMPORTANT: Ensure that maximum capacities are not exceeded. This is the most typical cause of appliance overload.

solution_steps.issue: The container is not securely locked on the motor base, preventing operation.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Place the motor base on a clean, dry, level surface such as a counter or table top.

2. Align and lower the Pitcher onto the motor base. Handle should be aligned slightly to the right of the “LOCK” symbol on the motor base.

3. Rotate the blender pitcher clockwise until it clicks in place. As the pitcher rotates, it will lower and the safety tabs on the bottom of the pitcher will slide under the safety tabs on the top of the motor base.

4. The pitcher can be placed on the motor base two ways; the handle can be on the front right corner or the front left corner.

solution_steps.issue: The lid is not securely on the container in the correct position, affecting functionality.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Holding the lid by the handle in the upright position, place it on top of the pitcher aligning the arrow ( ) located on the lid with the arrow ( ) located on the pitcher’s handle."
2. "Press the handle down until you hear a click."
3. "IMPORTANT: As a safety feature, the power button ( ) will flash and the motor will not work if the pitcher and lid are not installed correctly."
4. "When the pitcher and lid are installed properly, the power button ( ) will be solid, indicating that the appliance is ready for use."

issues: The container cover does not securely lock in place, preventing the appliance from operating.
The polarized plug does not fit into the outlet, and reversing the plug still fails to fit.
The food processor does not power on after being dropped or damaged.
The blade or processing disk is not properly placed before turning on the appliance, causing malfunction.
The control knob does not respond when trying to switch between different speed settings.
The food chute lid does not properly close, affecting the processing of food.
The appliance doesn't turn off even when the switch is set to the OFF (O) position.
The cord touches hot surfaces, potentially leading to damage or a safety hazard.
The food processor is used with attachments not recommended by the manufacturer, leading to potential risks.
The appliance fails to operate when the container is not correctly positioned on the motor base.

solution_steps.issue: The container cover does not securely lock in place, preventing the appliance from operating.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Align the base and bowl as illustrated in Figure 1. Align the bowl handle with the UNLOCK mark on the base. Turn the bowl counter-clockwise until it clicks onto the base. The bowl handle should now align with the LOCK mark on the base. The bowl handle will be positioned above the control buttons. There is only one position for the bowl to lock onto the base. The unit will not operate if the bowl does not lock onto the base.

2. Place the cover onto the bowl. Align the UNLOCK mark on the cover and the UNLOCK mark on the bowl as illustrated in Figure 2. Twist the cover counter-clockwise towards the LOCK until it clicks onto the bowl. The LOCK mark on the cover should now align with the LOCK mark on the bowl. 

3. Ensure that when the cover is locked into position, the safety mechanism on the cover and bowl align. The unit will not operate if the cover is not locked onto the bowl. 

4. Confirm that the bowl is locked into the base before attempting to lock the cover into position.

solution_steps.issue: The polarized plug does not fit into the outlet, and reversing the plug still fails to fit.
solution_steps.steps:
1. If the plug does not insert fully in the outlet, reverse the plug.
2. If it still fails to fit, contact a qualified electrician.

solution_steps.issue: The food processor does not power on after being dropped or damaged.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Do not operate the food processor with a damaged cord or plug or after the appliance malfunctions, or is dropped or damaged in any manner. 
2. Return the appliance to the nearest authorized service center for examination, repair or mechanical adjustment.

solution_steps.issue: The blade or processing disk is not properly placed before turning on the appliance, causing malfunction.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Be certain container cover is securely locked in place while operating appliance.
2. To reduce the risk of injury to persons, never place cutting blade on motor base without first putting container properly in place.
3. Unlock the bowl by turning it clockwise towards the UNLOCK mark and lift off.
4. Carefully remove the Shredding Disc.
5. Place the container properly on the motor base before placing the cutting blade.
6. Ensure that the bowl lid is twisted towards the LOCK mark to secure the cover.
7. Once everything is properly placed and secured, turn the knob to the desired speed position.

solution_steps.issue: The control knob does not respond when trying to switch between different speed settings.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Ensure that the appliance is plugged into an electric outlet, as stated: "Plug the cord into an electric outlet."

2. Verify that the large bowl is properly locked onto the base, as instructed: "Lock the large bowl onto base."

3. Confirm that the small work bowl is inserted and properly seated into the large work bowl: "Insert Small work bowl into large work bowl and twist inner bowl until it is seated into the large work bowl."

4. Check that the cover is securely locked in place: "Lock cover onto bowl."

5. Make sure the Food Chute Lid is locked: "Lock the Food Chute Lid."

6. Confirm that the container cover is securely locked in place while operating the appliance: "Be certain container cover is securely locked in place while operating appliance."

7. Attempt to turn the control knob to the desired speed position or the PULSE position for short processing tasks: "Turn the knob to the desired speed position for continuous processing or the PULSE position for short processing tasks."

8. If the knob still does not respond, ensure that the appliance is in the OFF (O) position when not in use: "Processor should always be left in the OFF (O) position when not in use."

9. Check the polarized plug connection: "To reduce the risk of electric shock, as a safety feature, this plug will fit in a polarized outlet only one way. If the plug does not insert fully in the outlet, reverse the plug."

10. If the control knob continues to be unresponsive, contact a qualified electrician, as suggested: "If it still fails to fit, contact a qualified electrician."

solution_steps.issue: The food chute lid does not properly close, affecting the processing of food.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Ensure the unit is OFF (O) and unplug the cord, as noted: "NOTE: Before opening Food Chute lid, turn the unit OFF (O) and unplug the cord."

2. Confirm that the Food Chute lid hinges onto the back of the Food Chute properly: "1 The Food Chute lid hinges onto the back of Food Chute. As illustrated in Figure 3."

3. Pull up the Large Food Pusher: "2 Pull up the Large Food Pusher. As illustrated in Figure 7."

4. Pull back the Food Chute lid and Large Food Pusher: "3 Pull back the food chute lid and Large Food Pusher. As illustrated in Figure 8."

5. Push down the Large Food Pusher into the Food Chute: "2 Push down the Large Food Pusher into the Food Chute. As illustrated in Figure 4."

6. Push down on the tab of the Large Food Pusher to latch the Food Chute lid onto the Food Chute: "3 Push down on the tab of Large Food Pusher to latch the Food Chute lid onto the Food Chute. As illustrated in Figure 5."

7. Ensure that the cover is locked into position: "NOTE: When the cover is locked into position, the safety mechanism on the cover and bowl will align. The unit will not operate if the cover is not locked onto the bowl."

8. Verify that the bowl is locked into the base before attempting to lock the cover: "NOTE: BOWL MUST BE LOCKED INTO BASE BEFORE COVER CAN BE LOCKED INTO POSITION."

9. Ensure that the Food Chute lid is not being defeated by any interlock mechanism: "18. Do not attempt to defeat the cover interlock mechanism."

solution_steps.issue: The appliance doesn't turn off even when the switch is set to the OFF (O) position.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Switch Off (O) and unplug from outlet to disconnect appliance."
2. "Do not operate food processor with a damaged cord or plug or after the appliance malfunctions, or is dropped or damaged in any manner. Return appliance to the nearest authorized service center for examination, repair or mechanical adjustment."

solution_steps.issue: The cord touches hot surfaces, potentially leading to damage or a safety hazard.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Do not let cord touch hot surfaces or hang over table edges or counters."
2. "Switch Off (O) and unplug from outlet to disconnect appliance, before putting on or taking off parts, before cleaning and when not in use."
3. "An extension cord may be used if care is exercised in its use. If an extension cord is used, the electrical rating of the cord must be at least as great as the electrical rating of the appliance."
4. "The extension cord should be arranged so that it will not drape over the countertop or tabletop where it can be pulled on by children or tripped over unintentionally."

solution_steps.issue: The food processor is used with attachments not recommended by the manufacturer, leading to potential risks.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Read all instructions before use.
2. The use of attachments not recommended or sold by the manufacturer may cause fire, electrical shock or injury.
3. Switch Off (O) and unplug from outlet to disconnect appliance, before putting on or taking off parts, before cleaning and when not in use.
4. Do not operate food processor with a damaged cord or plug or after the appliance malfunctions, or is dropped or damaged in any manner. Return appliance to the nearest authorized service center for examination, repair or mechanical adjustment.

solution_steps.issue: The appliance fails to operate when the container is not correctly positioned on the motor base.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Align the base and bowl as illustrated in Figure 1. Align the bowl handle with the UNLOCK mark on the base. Turn the bowl counter-clockwise until it clicks onto the base. The bowl handle should now align with the LOCK mark on the base. (The bowl handle will be positioned above the control buttons).

2. Note: There is only one position for the bowl to lock onto the base. The unit will not operate if the bowl does not lock onto the base.

3. Place the cover onto the bowl. Align the UNLOCK mark on the cover and the UNLOCK mark on the bowl (as illustrated in Figure 2). Twist the cover counter-clockwise towards the LOCK until it clicks onto the bowl. The LOCK mark on the cover should now align with the LOCK mark on the bowl.

4. Note: When the cover is locked into position, the safety mechanism on the cover and bowl will align. The unit will not operate if the cover is not locked onto the bowl.

issues: Food is unevenly processed due to not cutting ingredients into 2.5cm pieces.
Motor slows down when kneading dough because the amount of dough exceeds maximum capacity.
Slices are slanted or uneven if food is not placed evenly in the feed chute.
Food falls over in the feed chute when it's not packed full or incorrectly positioned.
French fries cutter becomes blocked, requiring clearing before processing more potatoes.
Malfunction of the processing bowl’s auto switch occurs if the processing lid is left in the locked position when not in use.
Ingredients need to be processed in batches to avoid overloading.
Some food remains on top of the disc after processing, which is considered normal.
The appliance should not be used if the power supply cord, plug, or appliance is damaged.
This appliance should not be used by children or persons without proper supervision or instruction.

solution_steps.issue: Food is unevenly processed due to not cutting ingredients into 2.5cm pieces.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Ingredients should be cut evenly into 2.5cm pieces before processing."

2. "Trim and cut food into 2.5cm cubes."

3. "Process no more than 7 cups at a time using the PULSE button at 1–2 second intervals until chopped to desired size or consistency."

4. "Avoid over-processing by checking the consistency frequently."

5. "If necessary, turn the POWER off and use a spatula to scrape down the sides of the bowl to encourage even processing."

solution_steps.issue: Motor slows down when kneading dough because the amount of dough exceeds maximum capacity.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Amount of dough may exceed maximum capacity. Remove half and process in two batches."

2. "If motor speeds up, continue processing. If not, add more flour, 1 tablespoon at a time until the motor speeds up."

3. "Process until dough cleans the side of the processing bowl."

solution_steps.issue: Slices are slanted or uneven if food is not placed evenly in the feed chute.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Place evenly cut food into the feed chute.
2. Apply even pressure on the pusher.

solution_steps.issue: Food falls over in the feed chute when it's not packed full or incorrectly positioned.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "The large feed chute must be packed full for best results."
2. "If processing smaller quantities, place items to the far left in the feed chute, or use the small feed chute, depending on the food size."
3. "Smaller ingredients: For long thin foods such as carrots, cucumbers, zucchini, etc., use the small feed chute. This will avoid the ingredient from tipping over during slicing."
4. "Larger ingredients: The wide feed chute is 14cm wide, and can fit ingredients up to this size. The chute can be packed to fill the width of the chute. The food should fit snugly so it is supported in an upright position in the chute, but not so tight that it could prevent the food from moving down the chute."
5. "Round fruit and vegetables: Prepare fruit or vegetables by washing and peeling (if necessary). Small fruit and vegetables should be trimmed on one end so the food sits flat inside the feed chute. Large fruit and vegetables may need to be cut in half to fit in the chute."
6. "Long fruit and vegetables: Prepare fruit or vegetables by washing and peeling (if necessary). Ingredients can be cut cross-sectionally to create circular results. Use the small and medium feed chute, or pack ingredients vertically in the large feed chute."

solution_steps.issue: French fries cutter becomes blocked, requiring clearing before processing more potatoes.
solution_steps.steps: 1. Always clear any blocked potato before processing more potatoes.

solution_steps.issue: Malfunction of the processing bowl’s auto switch occurs if the processing lid is left in the locked position when not in use.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Do not place the processing lid in the locked position when the appliance is not in use. (Refer to WARNING section: "To avoid possible malfunction of the processing bowl’s auto switch, do not place the processing lid in the locked position when the appliance is not in use.")
2. If the processing lid is left in the locked position, unlock it by holding the chute and turning it counterclockwise until the lid and handle parts no longer align, and the safety interlocking catch is disengaged. (Refer to Assembly section: "To LOCK the lid, hold the chute and turn clockwise so that the handle parts align.")
3. Ensure that the processing bowl, lid, and large pusher are correctly assembled before operating the appliance to engage the safety interlock and allow the motor to run. (Refer to OPERATION section: "The food processor will only operate when the processing bowl, lid and large pusher are correctly assembled. This engages the safety interlock, and allows the motor to run.")

solution_steps.issue: Ingredients need to be processed in batches to avoid overloading.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Ingredients should be processed in batches to avoid overloading."
2. "Place all ingredients in the bowl, starting with liquids, and being careful not to exceed the MAX LIQUID level."
3. "Process using the PULSE button until folded evenly."
4. "Do not over-process."
5. "Scrape down sides of bowl as needed."
6. "If processing smaller quantities, place items to the far left in the feed chute, or use the small feed chute, depending on the food size."
7. "Always remember to place the spindle and dough blade into the processing bowl before adding the food."

solution_steps.issue: Some food remains on top of the disc after processing, which is considered normal.
solution_steps.steps: 1. "It is normal for small pieces to remain after processing."

solution_steps.issue: The appliance should not be used if the power supply cord, plug, or appliance is damaged.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "It is recommended to regularly inspect the appliance."
2. "Do not use the appliance if power supply cord, plug or appliance becomes damaged in any way."
3. "Return the entire appliance to the nearest authorised Breville Service Centre for examination and/or repair."
4. "All maintenance (other than cleaning) is to be done by an authorised Breville Service Centre."
5. "Authorised Breville Service Centres can be found on our website www.Breville.com.au Alternatively, you can contact [Contact details as per the manual]."

solution_steps.issue: This appliance should not be used by children or persons without proper supervision or instruction.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "This appliance shall not be used by children. Keep the appliance and its cord out of reach of children."
2. "Children shall not play with the appliance."
3. "Appliances can be used by persons with reduced physical, sensory or mental capabilities or lack of experience and knowledge if they have been given supervision or instruction concerning use of the appliance in a safe way and understand the hazards involved."
4. "Cleaning and user maintenance shall not be made by children without supervision."

issues: The appliance does not turn on even when plugged in.
The blades or discs do not move during operation.
The appliance stops working during use and won't restart.
The lid does not lock securely, preventing the processor from operating.
The food processor makes an unusual noise when in use.
The food processor vibrates excessively when processing food.
The cord is damaged or frayed, posing a risk of electrical shock.
The food processor is difficult to clean due to food getting stuck in crevices.
The appliance emits a burning smell during operation.
The processor's attachments do not fit securely onto the base.

solution_steps.issue: The appliance does not turn on even when plugged in.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Make sure the work bowl and work bowl cover are properly locked on the base.

2. See if the Food Processor is plugged into a proper electrical outlet. If it is, unplug the Food Processor, then plug it into the same outlet again.

3. If the Food Processor still does not work, check the fuse or circuit breaker on the electrical circuit the Food Processor is connected to and make sure the circuit is closed.

4. If the problem cannot be corrected with the steps in this section, see the KitchenAid Warranty and Service section on pages 53-54. Do not return the Food Processor to the retailer – they do not provide service.

solution_steps.issue: The blades or discs do not move during operation.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Ensure the bowl is properly placed: "To reduce the risk of injury, never place cutting blade or discs on base without first putting bowl properly in place."
2. Verify the cover is securely locked: "Be certain cover is securely locked in place before operating appliance."
3. Make sure the mini bowl is correctly positioned if using it: "Place the mini bowl inside the work bowl over the power shaft. Rotate the mini bowl until it falls into place. When properly seated in the work bowl, the mini bowl cannot be rotated."
4. Check that the blades or discs are properly assembled: "Rotate the blade so it falls into place on the shaft" and "Fit the disc over the metal pin on the disc stem, then rotate the disc until it falls fully onto the stem."
5. Avoid processing too hard or overfilled food: "Never process any food that is so hard or firmly frozen that it cannot be pierced with the tip of a sharp knife" and "Do not overfill work bowl or mini bowl."

solution_steps.issue: The appliance stops working during use and won't restart.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "If the Food Processor shuts off while it is running: The Food Processor may be overheated. If the motor exceeds a certain temperature, it will automatically shut off to prevent damage."

2. "Press the Off Button and wait 15 minutes for the Food Processor to cool before resuming."

3. "If the Food Processor still refuses to run, wait an additional 15 minutes for the Food Processor to cool."

4. "If the problem cannot be corrected with the steps in this section, see the KitchenAid Warranty and Service section on pages 53-54. Do not return the Food Processor to the retailer – they do not provide service."

solution_steps.issue: The lid does not lock securely, preventing the processor from operating.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Make sure the work bowl is properly locked on the base. The manual states: "NOTE: Do not attach the cover to the work bowl before the work bowl is locked on the base. Damage to the work bowl may result."

2. Position the work bowl with the feed tube just to the left of the work bowl handle.

3. Grasp the feed tube and turn the cover to the right until it locks into place. The manual instructs: "Grasp the feed tube and turn the cover to the right until it locks into place."

4. Ensure that the work bowl and work bowl cover are properly locked on the base, as the manual notes: "NOTE: Your Food Processor will not operate unless the work bowl and work bowl cover are properly locked on the base."

5. Do not remove the work bowl from the base without first removing the work bowl cover to avoid damage: "Do not remove the work bowl from the base without first removing the work bowl cover. Damage to the work bowl may result."

solution_steps.issue: The food processor makes an unusual noise when in use.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Read all instructions."
2. "Avoid contacting moving parts."
3. "Close supervision is necessary when any appliance is used by or near children."
4. "Unplug from the outlet when not in use, before putting on or taking off parts, and before cleaning."
5. "Make sure the work bowl and work bowl cover are properly locked on the base."
6. "See if the Food Processor is plugged into a proper electrical outlet."
7. "The use of attachments not recommended or sold by the manufacturer may cause fire, electric shock or injury."
8. "Never process any food that is so hard or firmly frozen that it cannot be pierced with the tip of a sharp knife. Hard food can cause damage to the blade or motor."
9. "If a piece of hard food, such as carrot, becomes wedged or stuck on the blade, stop the processor and remove the blade. Carefully remove food from the blade."
10. "Do not overfill work bowl or mini bowl."

solution_steps.issue: The food processor vibrates excessively when processing food.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Never process any food that is so hard or firmly frozen that it cannot be pierced with the tip of a sharp knife. Hard food can cause damage to the blade or motor. If a piece of hard food, such as carrot, becomes wedged or stuck on the blade, stop the processor and remove the blade. Carefully remove food from the blade.

2. Do not overfill work bowl or mini bowl. For thin mixtures, fill work bowl up to 1⁄2 to 2⁄3 full. For thicker mixtures, fill work bowl up to 3⁄4 full. For liquids, fill up to the maximum level as described on page 10. When chopping, the work bowl should be no more than 1⁄3 to 1⁄2 full. Use the mini bowl for up to 1 cup of liquid or 1⁄2 cup solids.

3. Ensure that the work bowl and work bowl cover are properly locked on the base.

4. Make sure the Food Processor is plugged into a proper electrical outlet. If it is, unplug the Food Processor, then plug it into the same outlet again. If the Food Processor still does not work, check the fuse or circuit breaker on the electrical circuit the Food Processor is connected to and make sure the circuit is closed.

solution_steps.issue: The cord is damaged or frayed, posing a risk of electrical shock.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Do not operate any appliance with a damaged cord or plug, or after the appliance malfunctions, or is dropped or damaged in any manner. Return appliance to the nearest Authorized Service Facility for examination, repair, or electrical or mechanical adjustment."
2. "If the problem cannot be corrected with the steps in this section, see the KitchenAid Warranty and Service section on pages 53-54. Do not return the Food Processor to the retailer – they do not provide service."

solution_steps.issue: The food processor is difficult to clean due to food getting stuck in crevices.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Press the Off Button and unplug the Food Processor before cleaning.
2. Wipe the base and cord with a warm, sudsy cloth, and wipe clean with a damp cloth. Dry with a soft cloth. Do not use abrasive cleansers or scouring pads.
3. All the other parts of the Food Processor are dishwasher safe. Be sure to load them away from exposed heating elements in the dishwasher. If washing the Food Processor parts by hand, avoid the use of abrasive cleansers or scouring pads. They may scratch or cloud the work bowl and cover. Thoroughly dry all parts after washing.
4. After removing the work bowl cover, place it upside down on the counter. This will help keep the counter clean.
5. If any plastic parts should discolor due to the types of food processed, clean them with lemon juice.

solution_steps.issue: The appliance emits a burning smell during operation.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Unplug from the outlet when not in use, before putting on or taking off parts, and before cleaning.
2. Do not operate any appliance with a damaged cord or plug, or after the appliance malfunctions, or is dropped or damaged in any manner. Return appliance to the nearest Authorized Service Facility for examination, repair, or electrical or mechanical adjustment.
3. If the problem cannot be corrected with the steps in this section, see the KitchenAid Warranty and Service section on pages 53-54. Do not return the Food Processor to the retailer – they do not provide service.

solution_steps.issue: The processor's attachments do not fit securely onto the base.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Make sure the work bowl is properly locked on the base: "NOTE: Do not attach the cover to the work bowl before the work bowl is locked on the base. Damage to the work bowl may result."

2. Ensure the work bowl cover is correctly attached: "Grasp the feed tube and turn the cover to the right until it locks into place."

3. Verify that the work bowl and work bowl cover are properly locked on the base: "NOTE: Your Food Processor will not operate unless the work bowl and work bowl cover are properly locked on the base."

4. Avoid removing the work bowl from the base without first removing the work bowl cover: "Do not remove the work bowl from the base without first removing the work bowl cover. Damage to the work bowl may result."

issues: The ON/OFF light flashes indicating the water purifier is flushing.
Pro 400: The need to replace FILTER I when the water purifier signals.
Pro 600: The need to replace FILTER I and II when notified by the water purifier.
The inlet water pressure is too low, causing the water purifier to stop.
Pro 400: The requirement to replace FILTER II due to system performance issues.
Pro 600: The requirement to replace both FILTER I and II due to system performance issues.
The Inlet Grid Filter is blocked, preventing proper water flow.
The water purifier does not restart automatically after low water pressure is resolved.
The user is unaware that the "PURIFICATION LEVEL II or LEVEL III" light must turn green before using the purified water.
The water purifier's emergency stop is engaged, requiring a manual reset.

solution_steps.issue: The ON/OFF light flashes indicating the water purifier is flushing.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Allow the flush to be completed before using the water purifier. 
2. If the ON/OFF light continues to flash, replace the filters as specified: 
   - For Pro 400: Replace FILTER I.
   - For Pro 600: Replace FILTER I and II. 
3. If the problem persists, check if the Inlet Grid Filter is blocked and refer to the Complete User manual for further assistance.
4. Ensure the inlet water tubing is the proper size as specified in the “REQUIREMENTS FOR INLET WATER to purifier”.
5. If the inlet water pressure is too low and the water purifier has stopped, it will attempt to restart automatically. Ensure the inlet conditions are met for the purifier to function correctly.

solution_steps.issue: Pro 400: The need to replace FILTER I when the water purifier signals.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Observe the control panel of the Pro 400 water purifier. If the FILTER I light is on, it indicates the need to replace FILTER I.

2. To address the issue, refer to the manual section that states: "Pro 400: Replace FILTER I."

3. Follow any additional instructions provided in the Complete User Manual accessible at www.bluewatergroup.com for detailed guidance on how to replace FILTER I.

4. Ensure that after replacing FILTER I, the water purifier is properly reassembled and connected to power.

5. If the issue persists or if further assistance is needed, consult the Complete User Manual or contact your Bluewater dealer for support.

solution_steps.issue: Pro 600: The need to replace FILTER I and II when notified by the water purifier.
solution_steps.steps:
1. When the FILTER I or FILTER II light is on, it indicates that you need to replace FILTER I and II for the Pro 600.
2. Refer to the part numbers for the replacement filters: 
   - FILTER I, Pro 600: Carbon Block 919240005
   - FILTER II, Pro 600: Carbon Block 919240005
3. Ensure you have the correct replacement filters before beginning the process.
4. If the ON/OFF light flashes, indicating the purifier is flushing, allow the flush to complete before proceeding with the replacement.
5. Disconnect the Pro 600 water purifier from power to ensure safety.
6. Replace the FILTER I and FILTER II with the replacement parts as specified.
7. After replacing the filters, reconnect the water purifier to power.
8. Press and hold the Button for 3 seconds to reset the emergency stop if necessary.
9. Ensure that the FILTER I light and STOP light go out, indicating successful replacement and reset.
10. If further issues persist, see the Complete User manual on www.bluewatergroup.com.

solution_steps.issue: The inlet water pressure is too low, causing the water purifier to stop.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Make sure that the inlet water pressure is sufficient. If necessary, replace the filters. See Complete User manual. 
2. Install a pressure boosting pump to increase the inlet water pressure.
3. Check the parts that may influence the inlet water pressure. This includes the inlet water line, the Inlet Grid Filter, FILTER I, or any External Filters placed in front of Pro.
4. Make sure the inlet water tubing is the proper size specified in the "REQUIREMENTS FOR INLET WATER to puriﬁer".
5. If the water purifier has stopped, it will try to restart automatically.
6. Press and hold the Button to restart the water purifier. Release the Button when the FILTER I light and STOP light go out.

solution_steps.issue: Pro 400: The requirement to replace FILTER II due to system performance issues.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Locate the FILTER II indicator on the Pro 400 control panel. If it is on, this indicates the need to replace FILTER II. Refer to the manual: "FILTER II On: Pro 400: Replace FILTER II."

2. Ensure the Pro 400 is disconnected from power before attempting to replace FILTER II for safety purposes. The manual advises: "If Pro stops because of an emergency, disconnect it from power and connect it again."

3. Access the Complete User Manual on www.bluewatergroup.com for specific instructions on how to replace FILTER II if needed: "See Complete User manual."

4. Once FILTER II has been replaced, reconnect the Pro 400 to power.

5. Press and hold the Button to restart the water purifier. The manual states: "Press and hold the Button to restart the water purifier. Release the Button when the FILTER I light and STOP light go out."

solution_steps.issue: Pro 600: The requirement to replace both FILTER I and II due to system performance issues.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Identify the issue: If the FILTER I and FILTER II lights are on, it indicates that both filters need replacement.

2. Prepare for replacement: Ensure the water purifier is disconnected from power by checking that the ON/OFF light is not lit.

3. Replace FILTER I and FILTER II: Pro 600 requires the replacement of both FILTER I (Carbon Block, part number 919240005) and FILTER II (Carbon Block, part number 919240005).

4. Reconnect the system to power: Once the filters are replaced, connect the water purifier back to power. 

5. Reset the system: Press and hold the Button for 3 seconds to reset any emergency stops and allow the system to recognize the new filters.

6. Verify the replacement: Ensure that the FILTER I and FILTER II lights are no longer on, indicating successful replacement.

7. Check purification levels: Confirm that either PURIFICATION LEVEL II or III is lit, indicating that the water is ready to drink.

solution_steps.issue: The Inlet Grid Filter is blocked, preventing proper water flow.
solution_steps.steps:
1. See Complete User manual.
2. Check the parts that may influence the inlet water pressure. This includes the inlet water line, the Inlet Grid Filter, FILTER I, or any External Filters placed in front of Pro.
3. Make sure the inlet water tubing is the proper size specified in the "REQUIREMENTS FOR INLET WATER to puriﬁer".

solution_steps.issue: The water purifier does not restart automatically after low water pressure is resolved.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Press and hold the Button for 3 seconds to reset the water purifier.
2. Make sure that the inlet water pressure is sufficient. If necessary, replace the filters.
3. Check the parts that may influence the inlet water pressure. This includes the inlet water line, the Inlet Grid Filter, FILTER I, or any External Filters placed in front of Pro.
4. Make sure the inlet water tubing is the proper size specified in the “REQUIREMENTS FOR INLET WATER to purifier”.
5. Once the low inlet pressure has been resolved, Pro can be restarted manually by pressing the Button for 3 seconds.

solution_steps.issue: The user is unaware that the "PURIFICATION LEVEL II or LEVEL III" light must turn green before using the purified water.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Be aware! Do not use or drink the water before “PURIFICATION LEVEL II or LEVEL III” light turns green. It can take up to 60 seconds before the water purifier indicates good water quality.

2. When the system has been on standby, turn on the faucet and let the water run until the "PURIFICATION LEVEL II or LEVEL III" light turns green before using or drinking the purified water.

3. Do not drink the water during “PURIFICATION LEVEL I”.

solution_steps.issue: The water purifier's emergency stop is engaged, requiring a manual reset.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Disconnect the water purifier from power.
2. Connect the water purifier to power again.
3. Press and hold the Button for 3 seconds to reset the emergency stop.

issues: FP3-2 system leaks when connected to the water supply.
FP3-K1 system's cartridge replacement causes water to flow at reduced pressure.
FP3-HJ-K1 system's water softening cartridge does not fit properly.
FP3-4 system's membrane element is difficult to install due to tight housing.
FP3-5 system frequently loses warranty coverage due to non-compliance with installation instructions.
FP3-3 system requires specific inlet water temperature not always achievable in all climates.
The system leaks after filter cartridge or membrane element replacements.
Inlet water pressure exceeds the recommended range, causing operational issues.
Using non-genuine replacement parts leads to poor performance.
The system's water supply adapter does not fit standard plumbing connections.

solution_steps.issue: FP3-2 system leaks when connected to the water supply.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Close your water supply valve. Open faucet valve to release pressure build-up in the system.

2. Unscrew filter housing sump from filter cap by hand or using wrench (FXWR1-BL). (Remember to use wrench perpendicularly to the filter housing).

3. Remove old filter cartridge.

4. Remove filter cartridge out of plastic foil and place it inside filter housing sump (pressing against the top of plastic tang to ensure its central location).

5. Lubricate filter housing o-rings, next turn the system 180 degree and lubricate filter cap o-rings.

6. Screw filter housing sump with filter cap using wrench (remember to use the wrench perpendicularly to the filter housing). Use the same procedures for the installation of remaining filter cartridges.

7. Ensure to spread white cosmetic Vaseline (not included in the set) on to O-rings (3 pieces) placed inside filter housing rims.

8. Check if all o-rings and cartridge are positioned correctly.

9. During cartridge installation, follow proper configuration as shown in Table 1 and pay close attention to labels with numeric values placed on the cartridges.

10. WARNING! To seal threaded connections, always use Teflon tape during installation (does not concern threads for plastic and faucet nuts). 

11. Ensure the system is secured from high pressures and rapid pressure changes caused by local water supply systems by installing a pressure regulator on the inlet of the system's water supply. 

12. The system's optimal performance pressure is 3.5.

solution_steps.issue: FP3-K1 system's cartridge replacement causes water to flow at reduced pressure.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Close your water supply valve. Open faucet valve to release pressure build-up in the system.

2. Unscrew filter housing sump from filter cap by hand or using wrench (FXWR1-BL). (Remember to use wrench perpendicularly to the filter housing). Remove old filter cartridge.

3. Remove filter cartridge out of plastic foil and place it inside filter housing sump (pressing against the top of plastic tang to ensure its central location).

4. Lubricate filter housing o-rings, next turn the system 180 degree and lubricate filter cap o-rings.

5. Screw filter housing sump with filter cap using wrench (remember to use the wrench perpendicularly to the filter housing). Use the same procedures for the installation of remaining filter cartridges.

solution_steps.issue: FP3-HJ-K1 system's water softening cartridge does not fit properly.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Unpack new cartridge out of plastic foil.

2. Place filter cartridge inside filter housing sump (pressing against the top of plastic stem to ensure its central location).

3. Spread white cosmetic Vaseline (not included in the set) onto O-rings (3 pieces) placed inside filter housing rims.

4. Screw in filter housing cap to filter housing sump and tighten it with wrench (remember to use the wrench perpendicularly to the filter housing).

5. If you cannot tightly screw the filter cap with filter housing sump, check if all o-rings and cartridge are positioned correctly.

solution_steps.issue: FP3-4 system's membrane element is difficult to install due to tight housing.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Shut off water supply valve. Open filter faucet to release pressure from the system.
2. Push in the flange and pull out flexible tubing. Remove UF membrane housing from mounting clips.
3. Unpack new UF membrane out of plastic foil and remove end plugs. Unscrew inlet and outlet connectors from the UF membrane.
4. Remove all layers of old Teflon tape and apply multiple layers of new one. NOTE! Ensure that Teflon tape is winded in the opposite direction to the direction connector will be installed.
5. Connect inlet and outlet connectors to the housing of new UF membrane. NOTE! Do NOT remove elbow connector after the installation has been started. Stopping and removing (unscrewing) the element may result in inadequate connection and water leak.
6. Insert flexible tubing (all the way) into both ends of UF membrane. Check if inlet/outlet tubings are correctly and firmly connected. Make sure the tubing is not bent.
7. Push in membrane housing into mounting clips.
8. Open water supply valve.

solution_steps.issue: FP3-5 system frequently loses warranty coverage due to non-compliance with installation instructions.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Close your water supply valve. Open faucet valve to release pressure build-up in the system.
2. Unscrew filter housing sump from filter cap by hand or using wrench (FXWR1-BL). (Remember to use wrench perpendicularly to the filter housing). Remove old filter cartridge.
3. Remove filter cartridge out of plastic foil and place it inside filter housing sump (pressing against the top of plastic tang to ensure its central location).
4. Lubricate filter housing o-rings, next turn the system 180 degree and lubricate filter cap o-rings.
5. Spread white cosmetic Vaseline (not included in the set) on to O-rings (3 pieces) placed inside filter housing rims.
6. Screw in filter housing cap to filter housing sump and tighten it with wrench (remember to use the wrench perpendicularly to the filter housing). Use the same procedures for the installation of remaining filter cartridges.
7. Remember to install the cartridges in the correct order. 
8. WARNING! During cartridge installation, follow proper configuration as shown in Table 1 and pay close attention to labels with numeric values placed on the cartridges.
9. Screw filter housing sump with filter cap using wrench (remember to use the wrench perpendicularly to the filter housing). Use the same procedures for the installation of remaining filter cartridges.
10. ATTENTION! If you cannot tightly screw the filter cap with filter housing sump check if all o-rings and cartridge are positioned correctly.
11. ATTENTION! Wash your hands thoroughly after completing the installation.

solution_steps.issue: FP3-3 system requires specific inlet water temperature not always achievable in all climates.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Ensure that the inlet water temperature is between +2C (+35F) and +45C (113F) as stated in the manual: "Inlet water temperature.................................................................................................... ....between + 2C (+ 35F) and + 45C (113F)."

2. If the water temperature is not within this range due to climate conditions, consider using a temperature control device, though this is not mentioned in the manual, it is implied by the need to meet the specified temperature range.

3. Verify that the installation and operation are performed by trained service professionals, as per the safety precautions: "Product may be installed only by trained service professionals."

4. Use only original replacement parts, filter cartridges, and accessories made by the manufacturer to ensure compliance with the instructions: "Only original replacement parts, filter cartridges and accessories made by manufacturer may be used."

5. If you are unable to achieve the specified inlet water temperature, consult with a trained service professional for further guidance specific to your environmental conditions, as the manual does not provide additional steps for climate variations.

solution_steps.issue: The system leaks after filter cartridge or membrane element replacements.
solution_steps.steps:
1. In case system is leaking, disconnect it from its water supply.
2. Close your water supply valve.
3. Open faucet valve to release pressure build-up in the system.
4. Unscrew filter housing sump from filter cap by hand or using wrench (FXWR1-BL). (Remember to use wrench perpendicularly to the filter housing).
5. Remove old filter cartridge.
6. Remove filter cartridge out of plastic foil and place it inside filter housing sump (pressing against the top of plastic tang to ensure its central location).
7. Lubricate filter housing o-rings, next turn the system 180 degree and lubricate filter cap o-rings.
8. Screw filter housing sump with filter cap using wrench (remember to use the wrench perpendicularly to the filter housing).
9. Use the same procedures for the installation of remaining filter cartridges.

solution_steps.issue: Inlet water pressure exceeds the recommended range, causing operational issues.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Ensure that a pressure regulator is installed on the inlet of the system's water supply, as stated in the manual: "Pressure regulator must be installed on the inlet of the system's water supply."

2. Verify that the pressure regulator is set to the system's optimal performance pressure of 3.5 bar (52.5 psi), as specified: "The system's optimal performance pressure is 3,5 bar (52,5 psi) - pressure regulator is set to this parameter by the manufacturer."

3. If a pressure regulator is not installed, purchase one using catalog numbers provided in the manual: "Regulator may be purchased separately - catalog nr. ADV-REG_K, ADV-REG-CR_K."

4. Install the pressure regulator as per the manufacturer's guidelines to ensure compliance: "Failure to install pressure regulator will result in loss of warranty for pressure-operated elements."

5. After installing the pressure regulator or making any adjustments, conduct a system flushing procedure before resuming system usage: "Please note that after installing the system, as well as after each filter cartridge and hollow fiber membrane replacements, and in the case of long inactivity of the system, system flushing procedure must be conducted before resuming system usage."

solution_steps.issue: Using non-genuine replacement parts leads to poor performance.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Use only genuine Aqua Market and Aquafilter replacement parts, filter cartridges and membrane elements.

2. In case of use of other manufacturers' parts, Aquafilter is not responsible for any damages caused in the course of product use.

solution_steps.issue: The system's water supply adapter does not fit standard plumbing connections.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Ensure that the water supply adapter is compatible with the specification provided in the manual: "Water supply adapter ................................................................................................ .........................................................................1/2".
2. If the adapter does not fit, verify if a pressure regulator is needed as the manual states: "Pressure regulator must be installed on the inlet of the system's water supply".
3. If the adapter still does not fit, check if the system model requires specific instructions: "only in model: FP3-HJ-K1, FP3-4, FP3-5".
4. If there is still an issue, consult with "trained service professionals" as mentioned in the manual: "Product may be installed only by trained service professionals".

solution_steps.issue: Water purifier does not connect to the app via Wi-Fi despite following the setup instructions.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Ensure that the BRITA Mypure Max Water Purifier is connected to a power supply and that the power supply is switched ON.

2. Download the BRITA Mypure Max App from the iOS or Android Store.

3. Open the App.

4. Click on "Get Started" to proceed to configuration.

5. Click on "Connect to BRITA Network" to join BRITA network.

6. Choose "Configure Wi-Fi" and select your preferred home Wi-Fi network.

7. Enter password of your selected Wi-Fi network and click on "Save" to connect the Water Purifier to the App.

8. Upon successful configuration, click on "Proceed". Now your Water Purifier is connected to the App and the Wi-Fi symbol in the Water Purifier display will start glowing and show “Connected”.

9. In case of unsuccessful configuration, the display will show ‘Not Connected’. Please repeat steps 5, 6, and 7 to reconfigure.

solution_steps.issue: The faucet battery needs frequent replacement, leading to potential interruptions in operation.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Replace the battery in the faucet LED indicator to reset the filter change reminder. The battery type is CR2032 and included with every set of RF-20 filters.
2. Unscrew the faucet handle.
3. Remove the plastic cap from the faucet handle.
4. Under the faucet handle, locate the black rubber battery compartment. Grasp it from the sides and pull down as shown.
5. Remove the old battery from the compartment by lifting the silver metal tab and sliding the battery out of the rubber casing. Wait 30 seconds for the residual energy to drain to reset the indicator.
6. Replace with a new CR2032 battery by sliding the battery under the silver tab, making sure that the “+” sign and CR2032 are facing out.
7. Push the black rubber battery compartment back up into the faucet handle.
8. Pull the plastic tab out from the battery compartment to activate the faucet indicator. The LED light will blink red once, blue once, and then will be ready to go.
9. After replacing filters, locate the filter change sticker chart and write down the date and filters changed on the chart. It’s important to track each filter change since the RO filter is on a different cycle than the other 3. Here’s the replacement cycle:
   - After 6 months: replace 3 filter set (RF-20) and replace faucet battery
   - After 12 months: replace 3 filter set (RF-20) and replace faucet battery
   - After 18 months: replace 3 filter set (RF-20) and replace faucet battery
   - After 24 months: replace 3 filter set (RF-20), the RO filter (RF-40), and replace faucet battery
10. Note: Brondell provides a new faucet battery replacement with each RF-20 filter set and a new filter change sticker chart with each RF-40.

solution_steps.issue: Difficulty in aligning the filter label and filter base during filter installation, causing improper setup.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Remove the front cover from the Circle as shown. Match this to the arrow on the filter base.
2. Turn the filter(s) to be replaced a quarter-turn counter-clockwise until the unlock arrow on the filter label lines up with the arrow on filter base above it. Pull down to remove.
3. Install the new filter by aligning the arrow indicators on the filter label and filter base above as shown. Push up.
4. Turn a quarter-turn counter-clockwise until the filter stops. The filter base arrow should now point to the “lock” arrow on the filter label.
5. Be sure when replacing the filters that you install the new ones in the correct location by referring to the color coded sticker on the machine and matching to the colored filter labels.

solution_steps.issue: The filter change indicator does not accurately signal when the filters need replacement.
solution_steps.steps: 1. The LED filter change indicator in the faucet works by tracking both time and water flow from the Circle RO system. When the faucet LED indicator begins to flash red, it’s now time to change the filters and reset the faucet indicator by replacing the battery. Note: a new battery is always included with the RF-20 filter replacement set.

solution_steps.issue: Users may forget to track filter changes due to the separate replacement cycles of the RO filter and others.
solution_steps.steps:
1. After replacing filters, locate the filter change sticker chart and write down the date and filters changed on the chart. It’s important to track each filter change since the RO filter is on a different cycle than the other 3.
2. Here’s the replacement cycle:
   - After 6 months: replace 3 filter set (RF-20) and replace faucet battery.
   - After 12 months: replace 3 filter set (RF-20) and replace faucet battery.
   - After 18 months: replace 3 filter set (RF-20) and replace faucet battery.
   - After 24 months: replace 3 filter set (RF-20), the RO filter (RF-40), and replace faucet battery.
3. Note: Brondell provides a new faucet battery replacement with each RF-20 filter set and a new filter change sticker chart with each RF-40.

solution_steps.issue: The system may not perform properly if the reverse osmosis component is replaced with one of different specifications.
solution_steps.steps:

2. Contact Brondell toll free at 888-542-3355 for any questions regarding the replacement specifications.
3. After replacing the component, test the product water periodically to verify that the system is performing properly.
4. Ensure that the replacement component is a certified treatment component for the effective reduction of total dissolved solids.
5. Only use attachments (accessories) recommended or sold by the manufacturer to maintain the system's performance and safety.
