solution_steps.issue: No water flow even when the appliance is powered and connected.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Turn on incoming cold water supply valve.
2. Straighten out the hose. If water flow is still impacted, replace the hose.
3. Ensure the water supply valve is open completely.

solution_steps.issue: Insufficient water flow due to bent or twisted tubing.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Straighten out the hose. 
2. If water flow is still impacted, replace the hose.

solution_steps.issue: Water tastes or smells bad, indicating expired filters.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Replace the filters, per the instructions on Page 15.
2. To insert the filters, first line up the arrow on the filter head with the arrow on the filter. NOTE: It is very important to install the filters in the correct order. Simply match the same label colors to the filter head labels. From left-to-right, the proper order is: 1) Sediment filter 2) Pre-Carbon filter 3) Carbon Block filter.
3. With the top and bottom arrows still lined up, insert the top of the filter into the housing and turn to the right, until the filter will not turn any more. The Filter Head arrow should now be lined up with the “dot” on the top of the filter.
4. Repeat the process for the Pre-Carbon filter and Carbon Block filter.

solution_steps.issue: Leak surrounding one of the hose connections due to improper insertion.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Ensure the hose is inserted completely into the quick connector.
2. If the end of the tube is damaged, cut the tubing off at the damaged area and connect the tube again, or replace the tubing entirely.

solution_steps.issue: Water supply valve not turned on all the way, affecting flow.
solution_steps.steps: 1. Ensure the water supply valve is open completely.

solution_steps.issue: Filter change reminder LED indicator not resetting after battery replacement.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Under the faucet handle, locate the black rubber battery compartment. Grasp it from the sides and pull down as shown.
2. Remove the old battery from the compartment by lifting the silver metal tab and sliding the battery out of the rubber casing. Wait 30 seconds for the residual energy to drain to reset the indicator.
3. Replace with a new CR2032 battery by sliding the battery under the silver tab, making sure that the words on the battery are facing out.
4. Push the black rubber battery compartment back up into the faucet handle.
5. The indicator will blink red once, blue once, and then the indicator will function as normal.

solution_steps.issue: Sharp decrease in water flow due to colder tap water temperatures.
solution_steps.steps: 1. If the water temperature decreases due to inclement weather, water will flow more slowly through the system than normal.

solution_steps.issue: Water leak occurring when the unit is placed on an uneven surface.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Use or place the unit on a level area and do not apply force to the unit. This may cause physical injury and/or damage to the product that may void your warranty."
2. If a water leak occurs, "turn the water supply valve off immediately."
3. Check if "there is a leak surrounding one of the hose connections."
4. Ensure "the tubing is not inserted into the quick connector completely. Ensure the hose is inserted completely."
5. If the end of the tube is damaged, "cut the tubing off at the damaged area and connect the tube again, or replace the tubing entirely."

solution_steps.issue: Water purification quality diminishes when filters are exhausted.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Replace the filters according to their scheduled replacement intervals. If one or more of the filters are exhausted, the purification quality will diminish."
2. "Replace the filters, per the instructions on Page 15."

solution_steps.issue: Water pressure rise during cold weather causing potential leaks.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Turn the water supply valve off if the filter system will not be used for an extended period of time.
2. Especially during very cold weather, the water pressure may rise and may cause a water leak.
3. If a water leak occurs while using the product, or the area around the product is wet, turn the water supply valve off immediately.

solution_steps.issue: No water comes out of the unit due to the faucet diverter/T-valve being closed.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Turn the valve on the faucet diverter to the side to route the flow of water to the filter unit then turn on cold water. 
2. For the under-counter T-Valve connection type, water should be diverted permanently to the unit once you turn the valve to the “on” position.

solution_steps.issue: The button on top of the unit is not working because the water pressure might be too high.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Verify if the water pressure is indeed high by checking if it is over 120 psi.
2. Consult a plumber if the water pressure is high (over 120 psi).

solution_steps.issue: Low volume of filtered water might occur if the water temperature drops dramatically.
solution_steps.steps:
1. If the water temperature decreases, the amount of filtered water decreases.
2. Ensure that the water supply valve is open. If it is closed, open the water supply valve.
3. Check if it is time to replace the filters. If necessary, replace the filters.

solution_steps.issue: Poor aftertaste or bad smell from water if the filters are not replaced periodically.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "If the product is not in use for a long time, the filter might be dried out. Flush the filters for 10 minutes."
2. "If the water still smells or tastes bad, replace the filters."

solution_steps.issue: Condensation on the product's main body due to high temperature or humidity levels.
solution_steps.steps: 1. Is the temperature or humidity too high? This is natural. Continue to use as normal.

solution_steps.issue: The unit may not function properly if installed in a non-level area or if force is applied to it.
solution_steps.steps: 1. "Use or place the unit on a level area and do not apply force to the unit."

solution_steps.issue: Water flow is restricted due to filters not being regularly replaced.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Replace the filters as they are not being regularly replaced at the specified times.
2. Write filter replacement date on filter change sticker found on top of each filter.
3. Flush the filters and system with continuous water flow for at least 10 minutes before first time use or after changing any of the filters.
4. Press the button on top of the unit to dispense water (into your sink) and let it run for 10 minutes to flush the system and activate the filters.

solution_steps.issue: The appliance may not work correctly if the water supply valve is closed.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Turn the valve on the faucet diverter to the side to route the flow of water to the filter unit then turn on cold water.

2. Turn the valve up to use faucet as usual.

3. For the under-counter T-Valve connection type, water should be diverted permanently to the unit once you turn the valve to the “on” position.

4. After turning on water supply, check all connections for any leaks.

5. Wait 5 minutes and check once more for any signs of leaking prior to proceeding to next step.

solution_steps.issue: It is unsuitable to use the filtered water for aquarium or fishbowl water exchange.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Refer to the manual's caution on page regarding water usage: "Do not use filtered water for the water exchange of an aquarium or a fishbowl."
2. Ensure that you have an alternative source of water that is safe and suitable for aquarium or fishbowl use.
3. Follow the guidelines or recommendations from your aquarium or fishbowl manufacturer or a professional aquarist for the correct water parameters and treatment required for your specific aquatic environment.
4. If unsure about the water quality, consider using a water testing kit to check the parameters such as pH, ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate levels to ensure the safety of the aquatic life.

solution_steps.issue: The appliance may not perform effectively if used with microbiologically unsafe water without proper disinfection.
solution_steps.steps: 1. Do not use with water that is microbiologically unsafe or of unknown quality without adequate disinfection before or after the system.

solution_steps.issue: Treated water has Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) levels outside the system’s performance guidelines.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Send treated and untreated water samples to a water analysis lab for testing. It is important to test both the treated and untreated water to determine system performance.
2. If the TDS is not within the system's performance guidelines, replace the prefilter, post filter, and RO membrane cartridges.
3. Ensure the water supply to the Reverse Osmosis system is within specifications. Increase water pressure, precondition the water, etc., as needed to conform before doing maintenance on the Reverse Osmosis system.

solution_steps.issue: Continuous water flow to drain and low or no water production.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Cause: Missing flow control insert in drain port. Correction: Make sure flow control insert is in place. See no. 12 on page 22.
2. Cause: Plugged drain flow control insert. Correction: Replace drain flow control insert. See no. 12 on page 22.

solution_steps.issue: Water leaking from the faucet airgap hole.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Inspect and eliminate restriction or plug in the drain side of the faucet airgap (3/8” black tubing).
2. Check that the drain line is routed properly. Refer to installation instructions for proper drain connection. See pages 5 & 9.

solution_steps.issue: Plugged drain flow control insert causing performance issues.
solution_steps.steps: 1. Cause: Plugged drain flow control insert. Correction: Replace drain flow control insert. See no. 12 on page 22.

solution_steps.issue: Missing flow control insert in the drain port.
solution_steps.steps: 1. Make sure flow control insert is in place. See no. 12 on page 22.

solution_steps.issue: Incorrect connection of the drain side of the faucet airgap leading to a restriction or plug.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Inspect and eliminate restriction or plug."
2. "Check that drain line is routed properly."
3. "Refer to installation instructions for proper drain connection. See pages 5 & 9."

solution_steps.issue: Need for periodic testing of product water to verify system performance.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Product water should be tested periodically to verify that the system is performing properly.

2. Send treated and untreated water samples to a water analysis lab for testing. 

3. It is important to test both the treated and untreated water to determine system performance.

4. If the TDS is not within the system’s performance guidelines, replace the prefilter, post filter, and RO membrane cartridges.

solution_steps.issue: Requirement to replace reverse osmosis component with identical specifications for efficiency.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Locate the model, date code, and serial number on the rating decal, which is found inside the cover. This information is critical for ensuring you obtain the correct replacement component.

2. Contact the manufacturer to acquire a replacement component. You can call Toll Free at 1-866-986-3223 or visit whirlpoolwatersolutions.com. Provide them with the model, date code, and serial number to get the reverse osmosis component with identical specifications.

3. Replace the reverse osmosis component with one of identical specifications, as defined by the manufacturer, to assure the same efficiency and contaminant performance.

solution_steps.issue: Proper installation requires a suitable drain point for waste water.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Locate the 1/4” red tubing on the Reverse Osmosis filter assembly. See Fig. 10.

2. Determine if this length is long enough to reach the drain point. Longer lengths of tubing (see parts list in back of manual) may be needed.

3. If longer tubing is required, disconnect the 1/4” red tubing and replace with an adequate length of tubing to reach the drain point. Refer to Step F later in the manual on how to disconnect and connect tubing.

4. Route the tubing to the drain point and secure at the end with a bracket (not included). See Fig. 11. Provide a 1-1/2” air gap between the end of the tube and the drain. See Fig. 11.

solution_steps.issue: Necessity for a remote interior location with a nearby water source and drain point for installation.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Read through the entire manual before beginning your installation."

2. "Your Reverse Osmosis Drinking Water System can be installed under a sink or in a remote location. Typical remote sites are a laundry room or utility room."

3. "The Reverse Osmosis Filter Assembly and storage tank may also be installed in a remote interior location away from the Reverse Osmosis Faucet. You will need a nearby water source and drain point. See Fig. 4."

4. "Check size and position of items for proper installation into location chosen."

5. "Review the tools needed list. See Fig. 5. Gather needed tools before proceeding with the installation. Read and follow the instructions provided with any tools listed here."

6. "Route the drain tubing to an existing drain in the house. A floor drain, laundry tub, standpipe, sump, etc. are suitable drain points. See Fig. 11."

7. "Always be sure to provide a 1-1/2” air gap between the end of the hose and the drain point. This will prevent water from backing up into the system."

8. "Locate the 1/4” red tubing on the Reverse Osmosis filter assembly. See Fig. 10."

9. "Determine if this length is long enough to reach the drain point. Longer lengths of tubing (see parts list in back of manual) may be needed."

10. "If longer tubing is required, disconnect the 1/4” red tubing and replace with an adequate length of tubing to reach the drain point. Refer to Step F later in the manual on how to disconnect and connect tubing."

11. "Route the tubing to the drain point and secure at the end with a bracket (not included). See Fig. 11."

12. "Provide a 1-1/2” air gap between the end of the tube and the drain. See Fig. 11."

13. "NOTE: A flow control insert is located inside the fitting that the drain tube connects to. See No. 12 on page 22. Leave this fitting in place."

solution_steps.issue: Continual water flow to drain and low or no water production due to a plugged drain flow control insert.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Replace the drain flow control insert. See page 21.
2. Periodically check the flow control to be sure the small hole through it is clean and unrestricted.
3. If the flow control requires service, review the exploded view in Fig. 27.
4. Assemble and disassemble as shown in the manual.
5. If the flow control remains in the manifold when the push-in elbow fitting is removed, you will need to remove the drain port’s collet and o-ring to retrieve it.
6. Remove the collet and o-ring from the fitting with a small screwdriver. Do not scratch the internal walls of the collet port. See Figs. 28 & 29.

solution_steps.issue: Missing flow control insert in the drain port causing continual water flow to drain.
solution_steps.steps:
1. "Make sure flow control insert is in place. See page 21."
2. "The flow control, located inside the push-in elbow fitting on the drain port of the Reverse Osmosis filter assembly, keeps water flowing through the membrane at the required rate."
3. "If the flow control requires service, review the exploded view in Fig. 27. Assemble and disassemble as shown."
4. "If the flow control remains in the manifold when the push-in elbow fitting is removed, you will need to remove the drain port’s collet and o-ring, as shown in the next section, to retrieve it."
5. "Remove the collet and o-ring from the fitting with a small screwdriver. Do not scratch the internal walls of the collet port. See Figs. 28 & 29."
6. "Clean collet port, lubricate with silicone-based lubricant, and insert the o-ring seal into the bottom of the port. See Figs. 28 & 29."
7. "Push the collet inward until it locks in place. See Figs. 28 & 29."

solution_steps.issue: Water leaking from faucet airgap hole because the drain side of the faucet airgap tubing is plugged or incorrectly connected.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Inspect and eliminate restriction or plug in the drain side of the faucet airgap (3/8" black tubing).
2. Check that the drain line is routed properly. Refer to installation instructions for proper drain connection.
3. If needed, see pages 7 & 11 for detailed instructions on connecting to the drain point.
4. Ensure there is a 1-1/2" air gap between the end of the hose and the drain point, as per Fig. 12. This will help prevent water from backing up into the system.
5. Verify that the tubing is not kinked and allows for smooth water flow.

solution_steps.issue: Water leaks at push connect fittings due to tubing not being cut square.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Use a sharp cutter or knife to cut the end of tubing. Always cut the tubing square. See Fig. 17.

2. Inspect the tube up to 1" from the end to be sure there are no nicks, scratches, or other rough spots. If needed, cut the tubing again. See Fig. 17.

3. Push tubing through collet, until it engages the fitting. 

4. Pull on the tubing to be sure it is held firmly in the fitting.

solution_steps.issue: Water leaks at push connect fittings because tubing is not pushed in all the way.
solution_steps.steps: 1. Push tubing in all the way. See pages 14 & 15.

solution_steps.issue: Incorrect drain line routing causing leaks at the faucet airgap.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Inspect the drain side of the faucet airgap (3/8" black tubing) to ensure it is not plugged, restricted, or incorrectly connected to the drain point.

2. Check that the drain line is routed properly by referring to the installation instructions for proper drain connection. See pages 7 & 11.

3. If the drain line is incorrectly connected, adjust the connection following the guidance in the manual. For under sink installations, install the drain adaptor onto your sink’s drain pipe above the P-trap as shown in Figures 8-10.

4. For remote location installations, route the drain tubing to an existing drain in the house, such as a floor drain, laundry tub, standpipe, or sump, as shown in Figures 11 and 12. Ensure there is a 1-1/2" air gap between the end of the hose and the drain point to prevent water from backing up into the system.

5. Consult local plumbing codes to ensure compliance with regulations regarding the type of drain installation used.

6. Verify that the drain tube is cut square and inserted all the way into the red collet fitting on the Reverse Osmosis filter assembly. See Fig. 17 and Fig. 18.

7. Pull on the tubing to ensure it is held firmly in the fitting. 

8. Secure the end of the tubing at the drain point with a bracket (not included) to maintain the air gap. See Fig. 12.

solution_steps.issue: Tubing not cut properly leading to water leaks at connection points.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Use a sharp cutter or knife to cut the end of tubing. Always cut the tubing square. See Fig. 17.

2. Inspect the tube up to 1" from the end to be sure there are no nicks, scratches, or other rough spots. If needed, cut the tubing again. See Fig. 17.

3. Push tubing through collet, until it engages.

4. Pull on the tubing to be sure it is held firmly in the fitting.

solution_steps.issue: Incorrectly connected drain lines resulting in water leaks.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Inspect the drain side of the faucet airgap (3/8" black tubing) for any plugs or restrictions. "Correction: Inspect and eliminate restriction or plug."

2. Ensure that the drain line is routed properly. Refer to the installation instructions for proper drain connection. "Check that drain line is routed properly. Refer to installation instructions for proper drain connection. See pages 7 & 11."

3. If the tubing is not cut square, correct this by cutting the tubing square. "Cause: Tubing not cut square. Correction: Cut tubing square. See pages 14 & 15."

4. Ensure that the tubing is pushed all the way in. "Cause: Tubing not pushed in all the way. Correction: Push tubing in all the way. See pages 14 & 15."

5. If the tubing is nicked, remove the nicked portion by cutting the tube to a shorter length and reinsert it in the connection. "Cause: Tubing nicked. Correction: Remove tube from connection. Remove nicked portion by cutting tube to shorter length. Reinsert in connection. See pages 14 & 15."

6. If the outer tubing surface finish is not smooth, remove the problem area by cutting the tube to a shorter length and reinsert it in the connection. "Cause: Outer tubing surface finish not smooth. Correction: Remove tube from connection. Remove problem area by cutting tube to shorter length. Reinsert in connection. See pages 14 & 15."

7. Leave the elbow fitting that the drain line connects to in place if removing the drain line. "If removing the drain line, leave in place the elbow fitting that it connects to. See page 21."

8. Provide a 1-1/2" air gap between the end of the hose and the drain point to prevent water from backing up into the system. "Be sure to provide a 1-1/2" air gap between the end of the hose and the drain point. This will keep water from backing up into the system."

solution_steps.issue: Plugged or restricted tubing causing poor water flow or leaks.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Inspect and eliminate restriction or plug in the drain side of faucet airgap (3/8" black tubing). Refer to the manual: "Inspect and eliminate restriction or plug. Check that drain line is routed properly. Refer to installation instructions for proper drain connection. See pages 7 & 11."

2. To address water leaks at push connect fittings, ensure tubing is cut square. Refer to the manual: "Cut tubing square. See pages 14 & 15."

3. Ensure tubing is pushed in all the way. Refer to the manual: "Push tubing in all the way. See pages 14 & 15."

4. If tubing is nicked, remove the tube from connection and remove the nicked portion by cutting the tube to a shorter length. Reinsert in connection. Refer to the manual: "Remove tube from connection. Remove nicked portion by cutting tube to shorter length. Reinsert in connection. See pages 14 & 15."

5. If the outer tubing surface finish is not smooth, remove the tube from connection, remove the problem area by cutting the tube to a shorter length, and reinsert in connection. Refer to the manual: "Remove tube from connection. Remove problem area by cutting tube to shorter length. Reinsert in connection. See pages 14 & 15."

6. Ensure the flow control insert is in place inside the elbow fitting that the drain tube connects to. Refer to the manual: "A flow control insert is located inside the elbow fitting that the drain tube connects to. Refer to Fig 27. Leave this fitting in place."

solution_steps.issue: Missing or improperly installed components leading to malfunction or leaks.
solution_steps.steps:
1. Inspect Shipment: Your Reverse Osmosis Water Filtration System is shipped complete in one carton. Remove all items from your shipping carton. Check all items against the packing list. Note any items lost or damaged in shipment. Note any damage to the shipping carton.

2. Keep the small parts in the parts bag until you are ready to install them.

3. If there are missing parts or damage, do not return the unit to the store. Please call Toll Free 1-866-986-3223 or visit whirlpoolwatersolutions.com. When you call, please be prepared to provide the model, date code, and serial number, found on the rating decal on back.

4. If there is a problem with water leaking from faucet airgap hole, check the drain side of faucet airgap (3/8" black tubing) for any plugs, restrictions, or incorrect connections to the drain point. Inspect and eliminate any restriction or plug. Check that the drain line is routed properly, referring to the installation instructions for proper drain connection.

5. If there is a problem with water leaks at push connect fittings, ensure that the tubing is cut square. If not, cut tubing square.

6. Ensure that the tubing is pushed in all the way. If not, push tubing in all the way.
